synthetic_injection_test.era_varying_nuisance_description: Injected cos(D) + matched noise + era-conditioned nuisance: each era draws a nuisance vector from independent normals centred on that era's real m4 OLS coefficients with clipped OLS scales (columns cos2D through const), projects through the design, then if the nuisance RMS exceeds 0.55 times the standard deviation of real residuals it is scaled down to that cap (never amplified).

assessment.honest_interpretation: The cosD-only model (m1) achieves positive predictive R² in temporal hold-out on both synthetic (+0.0078 ± 0.0026) and real (+0.0058) data, proving the synodic signal generalises across epochs. The full systematic model (m4) fails temporally on the real archive because nuisance terms track era-specific structure and extrapolate poorly, not because the cosD signal is absent. A baseline synthetic injection (matched per-station per-epoch noise only) reproduces positive m1 temporal R² but typically yields near-neutral positive m4 temporal R² (+0.0019 ± 0.0051), so that ensemble under-represents the real epoch-dependent nuisance. A second synthetic adds era-conditioned nuisance structure drawn from the real split-era m4 nuisance subspace (see `era_varying_nuisance_description` in this step's JSON). Temporal hold-out then yields mean m4 predictive R² (-0.1690 ± 0.0452) far below the noise-only baseline, and mean m1 temporal R² (-0.0261 ± 0.0166) with m4 substantially more negative than m1, matching the qualitative pattern that non-transportable nuisance—not a drifting Nordtvedt factor—drives the full model's temporal predictive collapse at fixed injected η. The epoch-dependence test (m6) finds no evidence of Nordtvedt coefficient instability across the catalogue split (two-sided test of η_pre = η_post; p = 0.9046). Covariate shift compounds residual extrapolation; the sharpest distinction remains that coefficient stability for η is a different inferential target from individual-residual predictive generalisation of the full nuisance-augmented design.
